docs.title: Teaching Philosophy
docs.text:
My teaching is student-centered. I aim to make complex mathematical frameworks approachable by building from intuition to formalism:

  1. Start with a concrete problem (a facility layout, a transit network) before the model.
  2. Decompose the mathematics into small steps students can check and reproduce.
  3. Connect theory to computation, so students see an optimization model solve.
  4. Assess for understanding, with low-stakes practice and timely feedback.

In one sentence

Students learn optimization best when they can see the problem, build the model, and test it themselves.
